doc: The Fallen Silver Drift (slug silver-drift-rescue) - slot 7 of the master-everyday-3 batch (THR-1840).
Brief: `Docs/plans/encounters/master-everyday-3-brief.md`.
Final packet: `Docs/plans/encounters/silver-drift-rescue-final.md`. Draft: `silver-drift-rescue-draft.md`.
plotHookRolled: hook.long_road, hook.masterwork_completion, hook.shifting_shape
plotHookTaken:  hook.shifting_shape - the mountain changes shape under the miners: the new drift broke
into old workings nobody had mapped, the roof came down, and the ground keeps moving
while the master reads it, props it and brings the men out.
Seed dice: p3 choice (dig through the fall, or around it through the old workings) - opposition beast
(hunger), read as the hungry mountain: the rock and the bad air, never a monster - agentRole
judge_asked_to_rule (the reeve asks the master to rule where to dig) - scale region (overridden
to the village and its mine; the brief's scale floor counts slot 7 as settlement) - setting
ruin, overridden to rural, surviving as the old workings the drift broke into.
--- The narrator's 12 questions, answered ---
1 P1 arrival?      Yes: {actor} comes up the mine track above {location}, sent for by the reeve.
2 P2 events?       The drift fell in; it broke into old workings; four miners are behind the fall,
knocking; the air behind a fall goes bad.
3 P3 one stake?    Choice (rolled): dig through the fall or around it, before the air runs out.
4 <=80 words?      73 / 80 (opening + step-0 spine).
5 Read aloud?      Report throughout; no interior sensation.
6 Stated?          "They are alive." "Behind a fall the air goes bad." Stated plainly.
7 Every sentence works? Challenge, test or outcome.
8 Nothing unintroduced? Drift, fall, old workings, miners, reeve in step 0; props, timber and loose rock
in step 1; the bad air, the passage and the Builders Fellowship in step 2.
9 One named person? {cast:reeve} in step 0, nobody named in step 1, {cast:miner} in step 2.
10 Stake in a sentence? Can {actor} bring the four miners out of the fallen drift before the air goes bad?
11 Cards verb+noun? Carry Faint Knocking, Remember Lost Tunnels, Harden Green Timber, Still Loose Rock,
Stir Dead Air, Rouse Weary Bodies.
12 Opening per class? rural, written.
--- Mechanical design block ---
Crux            A silver drift has fallen in on four miners, and the reeve asks {actor} where to dig before the air goes bad.
Shape           Query prize on a three-step read -> shore -> bring-out spine. stone 0.74 (continue_weakened)
-> stone 0.80 (continue_weakened) -> stone 0.84 (fail_action). Linear, branch count 0.
Consequence hand (binding): condition + membership. No swap.
condition - condition_attachment trait.condition.wounded on $cast:miner on every step's
failure: the fall comes down on the trapped men's side. Person-borne (not $here), so it
wires `condition`, not `place`. Not on $actor: the brief caps personal conditions on the
mortal, and a master's failure costs the name, never the body.
membership - membership_change join builders_fellowship ($actor, chronicle) on step 2
success: the Fellowship that holds the mine takes in whoever brings its people out.
Query prize     Step 2 rewardPool { possession: 1 } tagFilters [#stone, #tool]: a tool from the mine's
store, given by the miners in thanks (iron tongs, a master chisel, a salvage kit ...).
Standing        bond_change $cast:reeve +0.12 / -0.12 on step 2; -0.04 on step 0 and step 1 failure.
reputation_with $here +0.05 / -0.06 on step 2; -0.02 on step 0 and step 1 failure (backs
the critical_failure chips on every route: a critical failure at any step ends the action).
Cost channels   All specials essence-priced. No Heavy Hand, no rider, no Undertow.
Cool failure    No one dies. The mortal is not hurt, jailed or branded. Failure: the fall crushes a miner's
leg, the miners wait alive for another crew, and the reeve's trust is gone. Critical failure:
the fall comes down again on the miner, and the reeve tells the village the master read the
rock wrong. The cost is the name.
Ends warm       Success: all four out alive, the miners' gift, the Fellowship's rolls.
Gender          Reeve and miner are bound cast (reuse-first): prose never genders either.
Accepted limit  An early-step failure followed by a final success wounds the miner without a chip on the
success_at_cost page (the step afterimage tells it); success_at_cost can also be reached
by a near miss alone, so its page cannot claim the wound.
Systems         cast, rewards, conditions, factions, reputation = 5.
Not colliding   Stone masters: strike a vault's centering, bring water down a hill conduit. Stone experts:
shore a bell tower, mend a dyke. This one digs living men out of a fallen mine.

stakes.goal: bring the four trapped miners out of the fallen drift
stakes.risk: see the fall crush a miner and lose the reeve's trust
stakes.won: brought the four trapped miners out of the fallen drift
stakes.lost: left the trapped miners for another crew to bring out

template.name: The Fallen Silver Drift

openings.rural: {actor} comes up the mine track above {location}, sent for by the mine's reeve.

steps.narrativeTemplate:
The new silver drift has fallen in. It broke into old workings no one had mapped, and the roof came down behind four miners. They are alive. The diggers can hear them knocking. Behind a fall the air goes bad.

{cast:reeve} can send the diggers through the fall, or around it through the old workings, and asks {actor} to choose.
steps.criticalSuccessAfterimage: {actor} read the fall in an hour. The old workings ran around it under sound rock, and the diggers went in through them at once.
steps.successAfterimage: {actor} chose the old workings. Their roof was sound, and they ran around the fall to a few yards from the trapped men.
steps.successAtCostAfterimage: {actor} chose the old workings, but stood on the fall too long reading it. A second slide came down where they had stood, and the diggers lost the morning clearing it.
steps.failureAfterimage: {actor} chose to dig through the fall. The rock shifted when the diggers opened it, and a stone came down on {cast:miner} on the far side.
steps.criticalFailureAfterimage: {actor} sent the diggers into the fall, and it came down again on the far side, on {cast:miner}. {cast:reeve} called the diggers out and would not send them back on the master's word.

nudges.name: Carry Faint Knocking
nudges.effectLine: Make the trapped men's taps travel clear through the rock, so they show where the men lie.

bandProse.critical_success: The taps rang clear through the rock, and {actor} could point to the yard where the men lay.
bandProse.success: The taps came clear through the rock, from beyond the old workings' far end.
bandProse.near_miss: The taps came clear only by evening, after a day of guessing.
bandProse.failure: The taps rang through every crack at once, and seemed to come from all sides.

nudges.name: Remember Lost Tunnels
nudges.effectLine: Wake the oldest diggers' memory of the old workings, so they can name a path around the fall.

bandProse.success: An old digger remembered where the old workings ran, and drew them in the dust.
bandProse.success_at_cost: An old digger remembered the old workings, and remembered a man who died in them, and would not go in.
bandProse.failure: The old diggers remembered three different workings, and argued about all three until noon.
bandProse.critical_failure: An old digger remembered the workings wrong, and swore to it, and the reeve believed the old digger.

steps.narrativeTemplate: The diggers go in where {actor} said. Every yard they clear must be propped with timber before they clear the next, or the roof comes down on them too. Loose rock hangs over the whole length. {actor} must set the props as fast as the diggers clear.
steps.criticalSuccessAfterimage: Every prop {actor} set held. The diggers cleared the whole length in a day and a night, and the roof stayed up over all of it.
steps.successAfterimage: The props held. Loose rock came down twice between them and missed the diggers both times.
steps.successAtCostAfterimage: The props held, but {actor} took the timber from the hoist house to set them. The mine cannot lift ore until it is replaced.
steps.failureAfterimage: A prop gave way at the far end, and the last yard of roof came down. The rock fell on {cast:miner}'s side too, and the knocking stopped for an hour.
steps.criticalFailureAfterimage: The roof came down along half the drift, and the fall slid again on {cast:miner}'s side. The diggers got out, and {cast:reeve} would not send them back under the master's props.

critical_success.text: They found a sound path to the trapped men.

success.text: They chose the old workings, under sound rock.

success_at_cost.text: The diggers lost a morning to a second slide.

near_miss.text: They chose where to dig only after a long day.

failure.text: They sent the diggers through the fall itself.

nudges.name: Harden Green Timber
nudges.effectLine: Toughen the fresh-cut props, so they bear the roof longer than new wood should.

bandProse.critical_success: The fresh props took the roof's weight without a creak, all the way to the far end.
bandProse.success: The green props bent and held, where new wood should have split.
bandProse.near_miss: The props held only after two of them split and were set again.
bandProse.failure: The props held, and the rock between them did not.
bandProse.critical_failure: The props held so hard that the roof broke around them instead.

nudges.name: Still Loose Rock
nudges.effectLine: Hold the cracked stone above the drift in place while the props go in.

bandProse.success: The cracked stone overhead stayed where it hung until every prop was in.
bandProse.success_at_cost: The stone overhead held, but a slide at the side buried a digger's lamp.
bandProse.failure: The stone overhead held for a day, then came down all at once.
bandProse.critical_failure: The stone held until the diggers were deepest in, then let go.

steps.narrativeTemplate:
On the second night the diggers break through. The air behind the fall is bad, and a lamp will not stay lit in it. {cast:miner} and the three others are too weak to climb. They must be carried out through the narrow passage the diggers made, under a roof that will not hold much longer.

The Builders Fellowship holds this mine. It takes in whoever brings its people out.
steps.criticalSuccessAfterimage: {actor} got all four out on their feet, and the props held behind the last of them. {cast:miner} walked down to the village unhelped.
steps.successAfterimage: {actor} sent the weakest out first. All four miners came out into the daylight alive.
steps.successAtCostAfterimage: All four miners came out alive. The roof came down behind the last of them, and the new drift is lost.
steps.failureAfterimage: The air went bad before the men could be carried, and the fall slid again and crushed {cast:miner}'s leg. {actor} got the diggers out, but not the miners.
steps.criticalFailureAfterimage: The roof came down on the passage while {cast:miner} was in it. The diggers pulled the miner free with a crushed leg, and {cast:reeve} called everyone out of the drift.

critical_success.text: The props they set held the whole length.

success.text: The props they set are holding.

success_at_cost.text: The mine gave up its hoist timber for the props.

near_miss.text: Two of their props split and were set again.

failure.text: The roof came down on the last yard they propped.

nudges.name: Stir Dead Air
nudges.effectLine: Move the foul vapour out from behind the fall, so the men can breathe and the lamps stay lit.

bandProse.critical_success: Clean air came down the passage like a draught from an open door, and every lamp burned bright.
bandProse.success: The bad air moved off, and the lamps stayed lit long enough to carry the men out.
bandProse.near_miss: The air cleared only after the first lamp had gone out twice.
bandProse.failure: The air moved, and drew the bad air from the old workings in behind it.

nudges.name: Rouse Weary Bodies
nudges.effectLine: Put strength back into the trapped men's legs, so they can crawl part of the distance themselves.

bandProse.success: {cast:miner} found the strength to crawl, and the others followed.
bandProse.success_at_cost: The men crawled out on their own, and one of them fainted at the mouth of the drift.
bandProse.failure: The men found the strength to stand, stood too soon, and the passage roof cracked over them.
bandProse.critical_failure: {cast:miner} tried to climb out first, and brought the passage roof down.

traitVariants.factorLine: Being Careful, they test every prop before a digger stands under it.
Being Proud, they will not wait for the reeve's timber.

narrativeTemplates.initiation: A silver mine has fallen in above a village, and its reeve sends for a master to bring out the four miners behind the fall.
narrativeTemplates.success: The four miners came out of the fallen drift alive.
narrativeTemplates.failure: Another crew was sent for to bring the miners out, and the reeve no longer trusts the master's reading of rock.

fallback.overview: The rescue at the silver drift is over, and {location} waits to see what the mine does next.

reactions.label: Seal the old workings
reactions.intent: The mortal has the reeve wall up the old workings. The village sleeps easier, and the mine gives up the ore past the fall.

reactions.label: Prop a road for the crews
reactions.intent: The mortal sets props past the fall, so the mine can dig there. The reeve is grateful; the miners' families are not.

critical_success.overview: {location} rang its bell for the four miners when they came home. The miners give {actor} a tool from the mine's store in thanks.

changes.title: Taken In
changes.detail: {actor} is on the Builders Fellowship's rolls now.

success.overview: The four miners are back with their families in {location}. They give {actor} a tool from the mine's store in thanks.

changes.title: Taken In
changes.detail: {actor} is on the Builders Fellowship's rolls now.

success_at_cost.overview: The miners give {actor} a tool from the mine's store in thanks. {cast:reeve} is counting what the rescue cost the mine.

changes.title: Taken In
changes.detail: {actor} is on the Builders Fellowship's rolls now.

failure.overview: {cast:reeve} has sent down the valley for another crew to dig the miners out. They are alive behind the fall. The reeve sent for a master, and now has to send again.

reactions.label: Wait at the mine mouth
reactions.intent: The mortal waits at the mine mouth until the other crew brings the miners out. The miners' families see who stayed.

reactions.label: Leave before the other crew comes
reactions.intent: The mortal goes down the valley before the other master arrives, and does not watch another crew finish the work. The village marks who did not stay.

critical_failure.overview: The miners are alive, and another crew is coming up the valley for them. {cast:reeve} tells {location} that the master read the rock wrong.

template.description: A silver mine above a village has fallen in, and four miners are alive behind the fall. Someone has to say where to dig, prop the drift, and bring them out before the air goes bad.
